It solves the problem of providing the fragment shader with the precise start and end texture coordinates required for volume traversal without complex CPU-side ray-box intersection calculations [S2, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly describes a method to determine 3D texture coordinates for ray entry and exit points by rendering bounding volume faces with colors equal to their texture coordinates. It details a two-pass rendering process (Pass 1 for exit points on back faces, Pass 2 for entry points on front faces) that allows the fragment shader to obtain these coordinates. This approach avoids the need for complex CPU-side ray-box intersection calculations, as the GPU handles the determination of entry and exit points through rasterization and framebuffer operations.
